passages.text: Rid yourselves, therefore, of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.
passages.sermon:
Peter writes to Christians.
He tells them to change their lives.
He commands them to remove all evil from themselves.
He says, “Get rid of all malice.”
He says, “Get rid of all deceit.”
He says, “Get rid of all hypocrisy.”
He says, “Get rid of all envy.”
He says, “Get rid of all slander.”
passages.original: Ἀποθέμενοι οὖν πᾶσαν κακίαν καὶ πάντα δόλον καὶ ὑποκρίσεις καὶ φθόνους καὶ πάσας καταλαλιάς

passages.text: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation, now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.
passages.sermon:
Newborn babies need milk.
You are like newborn babies.
You must desire pure spiritual milk.
This milk is not mixed with anything false.
You need this milk to grow.
You grow in your salvation by this milk.
You have already tasted that the Lord is good.
passages.original: ὡς ἀρτιγέννητα βρέφη τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γάλα ἐπιποθήσατε ἵνα ἐν αὐτῷ αὐξηθῆτε εἰς σωτηρίαν εἰ ἐγεύσασθε ὅτι χρηστὸς ὁ Κύριος

passages.text: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight, you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the living stone.
People rejected Jesus.
God chose Jesus.
Jesus is precious to God.
You come to Jesus.
You are like living stones.
God is building you together.
God is making you a spiritual house.
God calls you to be a holy priesthood.
You offer spiritual sacrifices to God.
God accepts these sacrifices through Jesus Christ.
passages.original: Πρὸς ὃν προσερχόμενοι λίθον ζῶντα ὑπὸ ἀνθρώπων μὲν ἀποδεδοκιμασμένον παρὰ δὲ Θεῷ ἐκλεκτὸν ἔντιμον καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡς λίθοι ζῶντες οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικὸς εἰς ἱεράτευμα ἅγιον ἀνενέγκαι πνευματικὰς θυσίας εὐπροσδέκτους τῷ Θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: For it stands in Scripture: “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks in Scripture.
God says, “I lay a stone in Zion.”
This stone is chosen.
This stone is precious.
This stone is a cornerstone.
Anyone who believes in this stone will never be put to shame.
passages.original: διότι περιέχει ἐν γραφῇ Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἐκλεκτὸν ἀκρογωνιαῖον ἔντιμον καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ

passages.text: To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,” and, “A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.” They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the living stone.
God chose Jesus.
God considers Jesus precious.
You believe in Jesus.
To you who believe, Jesus is precious.
Some people do not believe in Jesus.
The builders rejected Jesus.
God made Jesus the cornerstone.
Jesus became the most important stone.
Jesus is also a stone that makes people stumble.
Jesus is a rock that causes people to fall.
People stumble over Jesus because they disobey the word.
God appointed them to stumble because of their disobedience.
passages.original: Ὑμῖν οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ Λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας Καὶ Λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ πέτρα σκανδάλου Οἳ προσκόπτουσιν τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες εἰς ὃ καὶ ἐτέθησαν

passages.text: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
passages.sermon:
You are a chosen people.
God chose you.
You are a royal priesthood.
You are a holy nation.
You belong to God.
God made you His own people.
God called you out of darkness.
He brought you into His wonderful light.
God did this so you would proclaim His virtues.
You should tell others about the goodness of God.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα ἔθνος ἅγιον λαὸς εἰς περιποίησιν ὅπως τὰς ἀρετὰς ἐξαγγείλητε τοῦ ἐκ σκότους ὑμᾶς καλέσαντος εἰς τὸ θαυμαστὸν αὐτοῦ φῶς

passages.text: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
passages.sermon:
You are the people of God.
You were not always God’s people.
In the past, you did not belong to God.
Now, you belong to God.
God has shown you mercy.
Before, you did not receive mercy.
Now, you have received mercy from God.
passages.original: οἵ ποτε οὐ λαὸς νῦν δὲ λαὸς Θεοῦ οἱ οὐκ ἠλεημένοι νῦν δὲ ἐλεηθέντες

passages.text: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.
passages.sermon:
You are beloved by God.
I urge you to listen.
You are foreigners and exiles in this world.
You do not truly belong here.
Abstain from the desires of the flesh.
These desires fight against your soul.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητοί παρακαλῶ ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν αἵτινες στρατεύονται κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς

passages.text: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.
passages.sermon:
You are the people of God.
You live among the Gentiles.
Live with honor among them.
Some Gentiles accuse you of doing evil.
They speak against you as if you are wrongdoers.
Let them see your good deeds.
When they see your good works, they will recognize them.
Because of your good deeds, they will glorify God.
They will do this on the day God visits us.
passages.original: τὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἔχοντες καλήν ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καταλαλοῦσιν ὑμῶν ὡς κακοποιῶν ἐκ τῶν καλῶν ἔργων ἐποπτεύοντες δοξάσωσιν τὸν Θεὸν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς

passages.text: Submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human institution, whether to the king as the supreme authority, or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.
passages.sermon:
God calls you to submit to every human authority.
Do this for the Lord’s sake.
Submit to the king.
The king holds the highest authority among people.
Submit also to governors.
God sends governors through the king.
Governors punish those who do wrong.
Governors praise those who do right.
passages.original: Ὑποτάγητε πάσῃ ἀνθρωπίνῃ κτίσει διὰ τὸν Κύριον εἴτε βασιλεῖ ὡς ὑπερέχοντι εἴτε ἡγεμόσιν ὡς δι’ αὐτοῦ πεμπομένοις εἰς ἐκδίκησιν κακοποιῶν ἔπαινον δὲ ἀγαθοποιῶν

passages.text: For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.
passages.sermon:
God has a will for you.
God wants you to do good.
When you do good, you silence foolish people.
Foolish people do not understand.
Your good actions stop their ignorance.
passages.original: ὅτι οὕτως ἐστὶν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας φιμοῦν τὴν τῶν ἀφρόνων ἀνθρώπων ἀγνωσίαν

passages.text: Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.
passages.sermon:
You are free people.
Do not use your freedom to hide evil.
Do not use your freedom as an excuse to do wrong.
Live as servants of God.
passages.original: ὡς ἐλεύθεροι καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐπικάλυμμα ἔχοντες τῆς κακίας τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἀλλ’ ὡς Θεοῦ δοῦλοι

passages.text: Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king.
passages.sermon:
Show respect to every person.
Love all believers as brothers and sisters.
Fear God.
Honor the king.
passages.original: Πάντας τιμήσατε τὴν ἀδελφότητα ἀγαπᾶτε τὸν Θεὸν φοβεῖσθε τὸν βασιλέα τιμᾶτε

passages.text: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.
passages.sermon:
Servants must submit to their masters.
Servants must show respect in every situation.
Servants must obey not only good and gentle masters.
Servants must also obey masters who are harsh or unreasonable.
passages.original: Οἱ οἰκέται ὑποτασσόμενοι ἐν παντὶ φόβῳ τοῖς δεσπόταις οὐ μόνον τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς καὶ ἐπιεικέσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῖς σκολιοῖς

passages.text: For if anyone endures the pain of unjust suffering because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.
passages.sermon:
God sees when a person suffers unfairly.
This person feels pain.
This person endures the pain.
This person does this because he is aware of God.
God approves of this endurance.
God considers this commendable.
passages.original: τοῦτο γὰρ χάρις εἰ διὰ συνείδησιν Θεοῦ ὑποφέρει τις λύπας πάσχων ἀδίκως

passages.text: How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.
passages.sermon:
If you do wrong, you may be punished.
If you endure punishment for doing wrong, you gain no credit.
If you do good, you may still suffer.
If you endure suffering for doing good, God commends you.
passages.original: ποῖον γὰρ κλέος εἰ ἁμαρτάνοντες καὶ κολαφιζόμενοι ὑπομενεῖτε ἀλλ’ εἰ ἀγαθοποιοῦντες καὶ πάσχοντες ὑπομενεῖτε τοῦτο χάρις παρὰ Θεῷ

passages.text: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps: “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”
passages.sermon:
God called you to this purpose.
Christ suffered for you.
He left you an example.
You should follow His footsteps.
Christ did not commit any sin.
No deceit was found in His mouth.
passages.original: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐκλήθητε ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ὑμῖν ὑπολιμπάνων ὑπογραμμὸν ἵνα ἐπακολουθήσητε τοῖς ἴχνεσιν αὐτοῦ Ὃς ἁμαρτίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ suffered for us.
People insulted Jesus.
He did not insult them in return.
People caused Jesus to suffer.
He did not threaten them.
Jesus trusted God.
God judges justly.
passages.original: ὃς λοιδορούμενος οὐκ ἀντελοιδόρει πάσχων οὐκ ἠπείλει παρεδίδου δὲ τῷ κρίνοντι δικαίως

passages.text: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ bore our sins.
He carried our sins in His own body.
He did this on the cross.
He did this so we would die to sin.
He did this so we would live for righteousness.
His wounds heal you.
passages.original: ὃς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αὐτὸς ἀνήνεγκεν ἐν τῷ σώματι αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον ἵνα ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ἀπογενόμενοι τῇ δικαιοσύνῃ ζήσωμεν Οὗ τῷ μώλωπι ἰάθητε

passages.text: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
passages.sermon:
You were like sheep.
You wandered and went astray.
Now you have returned.
You have come back to the Shepherd.
The Shepherd cares for your souls.
He is also the Overseer of your souls.
passages.original: Ἦτε γὰρ ὡς πρόβατα πλανώμενοι ἀλλὰ ἐπεστράφητε νῦν ἐπὶ τὸν Ποιμένα καὶ Ἐπίσκοπον τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν
